approach.method_basis: The reference being improved on is this node's Parent: a task-local evolutionary molecular optimizer with a Bayesian purchase step on top. It keeps every scored molecule of the current session in an archive and a 64-member score-ranked survivor population, and each round breeds a fresh field of 160 de novo offspring from that population by rank-biased crossover and one-to-three-step graph mutation, admitting them under a canonical-identity and duplicate check. It then decides which ten of those 160 actually get oracle evaluations with a Gaussian-process surrogate fitted on the session's accepted labels alone: a count-Morgan fingerprint kernel (generalized Tanimoto on environment counts) supplies a posterior mean and a full cross-candidate covariance over the field, one Cholesky factor of that covariance turns ten standard-normal rows into ten correlated draws of the whole field's value, and each row in turn buys the best still-available candidate under its own draw, with the winner masked out before the next row and ties going to the lowest pool index. That is Thompson-style sampled-maxima allocation over a generated pool. After three announcements without an improvement the eligible set narrows to the forty highest posterior means until an improving batch resets it. Earlier children of this lineage contributed the fingerprint-GP allocation itself, that stall-conditioned eligibility narrowing, the identity-admission rules, and most recently the removal of a source-relative sulfur admission gate, which is the state this Parent is in.
approach.novelty: Everything above is kept, including what a candidate is worth and how the batch is masked, and only one thing changes: the arrangement of the ten random inputs. Five rows are drawn and the other five are their exact negatives, so an announcement probes the posterior's two tails in mirrored pairs instead of sampling it ten times independently. This is a variance-reduced (antithetic) sampling design rather than a new acquisition rule, and because the standard normal is symmetric about zero each row keeps exactly the law it had before and the whole cross-candidate correlation structure is untouched, which is what makes any measured difference attributable to the design. What distinguishes it from the rest of this lineage's work on the same draw is that none of those arms touched the design: siblings attacked the redundancy from the price side with expected-improvement pricing, determinant and diversity reweighting, within-batch conditioning on fantasy labels and admission-level class quotas, and from the residual's amplitude (inflated, contracted, residual-calibrated, refit-disagreement) and its cross-candidate dependence; a historical antithetic experiment on an older host built a doubled scenario panel and a greedy expected-maximum criterion on top of it, which is a changed price. Here the price, the covariance factor and every marginal stay exactly as inherited and only the joint design of the ten rows differs.

observed_bottleneck: The one behaviour that limits this Parent is how its allocator spends an announcement: it buys ten of the 160 freshly bred candidates by taking the sequentially masked argmax of ten independent standard-normal rows pushed through a single factor of the pool posterior covariance, and those ten purchases come out markedly more alike than the field they were chosen from. Recomputed from the Parent's own fifteen published sessions and all 435 announcements, the mean fragment-excluded count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto similarity among the ten purchased identities is 0.7053990019444182 (population SD 0.07218100328900372) against 0.6071009079231077 over the 160-member fields: the buy concentrates where the field does not. The same draw is simultaneously the most load-bearing and the least controlled part of the method. Removing the sampled residual entirely costs -0.12689408391255833 (n-c4c934fd6a68), and marginal-preserving removals of its cross-candidate correlation each lowered the outcome, so the dispersion must stay; yet re-drawing it with no rule change at all moved matched panels from -0.021233356620171045 (n-7e8300237702) and -0.020451584507293008 (n-515ab49db6e0) to -0.0017351731423886536 (n-47993ce5d053) and +0.007747005070628643 (n-843b25e73dee), with single cells swinging up to 0.12. Ten independent rows are the highest-variance estimator of the posterior's maxima set available at that sample count, and the Parent (macro mean 0.613802723974122, +0.006772407762991002 over Anchor n-cf8d309c06de) inherits that uncontrolled channel unchanged, realizing an incumbent-increment mass of 6.079659193977185 over 4,350 purchases of which only 255 are nonzero. Every previous attempt on this redundancy changed the price or admission rather than the sample, including the incumbent-referenced expected-improvement pricing of the eligible pool (n-698a02f85be1, -0.05328817319169632) and the restricted-consumer arm n-1c2f17550a3e (-0.009887882129600714); the arrangement of the ten base rows relative to one another has never been touched.

adoptions.applicability: The borrowed element is the base-sample design only. This host's acquisition is a sampled-maxima rule rather than a differentiable MC acquisition, so no sample-average-approximation optimization, no fixed base-sample reuse across candidates and no gradient claim is adopted; the measured endpoint here is the redundancy of the realized purchases and then the matched macro panel.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Treating the base samples of a Monte-Carlo batch acquisition as a design whose variance can be reduced at a fixed sample count, instead of as independent draws.

deviations.adopted_setting: Exact antithetic pairing of the standard-normal base rows of a sampled-maxima allocation over a discrete generated pool.
deviations.paper_setting: Randomized quasi-Monte-Carlo (scrambled Sobol) base samples for a differentiable MC acquisition optimized over a continuous domain.
deviations.reason: Antithetic pairing is the one variance-reduced design whose marginals and whole cross-candidate covariance are provably the Parent's, so a measured difference is attributable to the design rather than to a changed law; a scrambled net would also change the realized marginals at this sample count and is left to the approach's declared follow-up.

deviations.adopted_setting: Fresh base samples are drawn per announcement from the inherited generator at the inherited control-flow point.
deviations.paper_setting: Base samples are drawn once and held fixed across acquisition optimization steps.
deviations.reason: This host performs no acquisition optimization loop; holding samples across announcements would change the inherited allocation law and is outside the frozen isolation.

adoptions.implementation_change: FingerprintPosterior.select no longer draws one (batch_size, pool) standard-normal array. It draws ceil(batch_size/2) rows from the inherited generator and forms the announcement's rows as those rows interleaved with their exact negatives, leaving the inherited residual expression, pool Cholesky factor, jitter ladder, numerical fallback, eligibility mask, sequential availability masking, first-index ties and pool width untouched.

adoptions.applicability: Only the plain antithetic coupling is taken. The paper's local antithetic constructions inside scrambled nets, its smoothness assumptions and its error-rate statements are not adopted or claimed: here the estimator is a ten-row sampled-maxima set over a correlated 160-dimensional Gaussian, and the question is empirical, whether the mirrored arrangement lowers the realized redundancy of the purchases on this host.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Antithetic coupling of sample points as the variance-reduction device, and the symmetry argument that makes the coupled sample keep the target law exactly.

deviations.adopted_setting: Plain exact antithetic pairs on the Gaussian base rows of a discrete allocation decision, with no net, no scrambling and no error-rate claim.
deviations.paper_setting: Antithetic constructions combined with scrambled digital nets, analyzed for integration error rates on smooth integrands.
deviations.reason: The frozen ticket isolates the base-sample design with the Parent's law preserved exactly; a net would introduce a second design element and a second mechanism in one node.

adoptions.implementation_change: Row 2k-1 is the drawn row z_k and row 2k is -z_k, formed as torch.stack((drawn, -drawn), dim=1).reshape(2 * pairs, pool)[:batch_size] and pushed through the unchanged score_scale * (normals @ factor.T); the per-pair negation identity and the realized marginals are logged as receipts.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the ticket's frozen Search Policy review r80-exhausted-axes-review under the recorded stagnation, with no new web search claimed and no new asset or dependency introduced. Two of its six sources bear on this node and are adopted: BoTorch's sample-average-approximation account of base samples licenses treating the announcement's ten rows as a design rather than as ten independent draws, and Owen's antithetic-sampling result supplies the exact construction, whose symmetry argument is what makes the change auditable as law-preserving. The review's own search found no source applying antithetic or randomized quasi-Monte-Carlo base samples to batch Thompson sampling over a generated candidate pool, so the step onto this allocator is this campaign's own and its endpoint effect is an empirical question here. The review's trust-region, latent-space, conformal and batch-size sources are not adopted: each would change the eligible region, the model or the cadence, which this frozen isolation excludes. No paper establishes an endpoint sign for this host, which is why the mechanistic endpoints are registered in front of the score.

sources.applicability: This Parent's buy is exactly a ten-sample Monte-Carlo estimate of the posterior's maxima set over a 160-member pool, with no variance-reduction design on its base samples. The paper licenses treating those ten rows as a design to be chosen rather than ten independent draws, while the acquisition objective, the covariance factor and the sequential masking it is paired with here stay as inherited.
sources.finding: Monte-Carlo acquisition values and their batch maxima are estimated from base samples, and the sample-average-approximation analysis covers randomized quasi-Monte-Carlo base samples: RQMC significantly reduces the variance of the estimate and of its gradient relative to independent draws at the same sample count.
sources.title: BoTorch: A Framework for Efficient Monte-Carlo Bayesian Optimization, Balandat et al., NeurIPS 2020

sources.applicability: Supplies the exact construction implemented here: exact antithetic pairing of Gaussian base rows, which by the symmetry of the standard normal preserves every marginal and the whole cross-candidate covariance, so the design change is auditable as law-preserving on this host. Scrambled nets are not adopted; the frozen review found no source applying antithetic or RQMC base samples to batch Thompson sampling over a generated candidate pool, so that step is this campaign's own.
sources.finding: Antithetic coupling of sample points, including in combination with scrambled digital nets, improves the error rate of an integration estimate, whereas control variates and importance sampling only change its constant.
sources.title: Local antithetic sampling with scrambled nets, Owen, Annals of Statistics 2008

hypothesis: One modification of the m-000000000006 consumer on code Parent n-f28be8ac3d12: an exactly antithetic base-sample design for the announcement's ten correlated function draws, replacing ten independent standard-normal rows by five mirror pairs. In FingerprintPosterior.select, after the unchanged feature lookup, the unchanged distribution call and the unchanged pool Cholesky with its inherited jitter ladder, pairs = (batch_size + 1) // 2 rows z_1..z_pairs are drawn from the inherited posterior generator in the inherited order at the inherited float64 dtype and device, and the announcement's row 2k-1 is z_k while row 2k is -z_k, truncated to batch_size rows. The residual matrix is still score_scale * (normals @ factor.T) with that same factor, the samples are still mean_tensor + residual, and the finite guard, the numerical fallback, the stall-conditioned top-posterior-mean eligibility mask, the sequential availability masking, the first-index tie rule, the pool width of 160, the announced batch of ten and every generator, admission, archive, survivor and population law are retained verbatim. By the symmetry of the standard normal each row keeps exactly the Parent's marginal law and, through the same factor, the Parent's whole cross-candidate covariance, so this is a sampling design and not a new pricing rule. Path of effect: within one announcement the two members of a pair sit on opposite sides of the posterior mean in every candidate direction at once, so where ten independent rows can repeatedly favour the same high-mean neighbourhood, five mirrored pairs spend half of their positions on the opposite tail of the same correlated field; the masked argmax of each row therefore lands on a less redundant set of ten identities, which is read as the fall of within-announcement purchased similarity, and a less redundant batch at equal oracle cost is the channel through which realized incumbent-increment mass and then the matched macro mean could rise. Strictly fewer standard normals are consumed and no new random number, oracle call, asset, package or state is introduced.

finding_summary.headline: Mirror-paired draws ran exactly in all 435 announcements, but the ten purchases stayed as alike as before and progress mass fell
finding_summary.insights: The base-sample design axis is now measured and it is not where this loop's within-batch redundancy lives. The design worked at the level it acts on and the effect is visible: the two purchases made by a mirror pair are 0.0055 less alike than two purchases made by unrelated rows of the same announcement, where the Parent's adjacent-row comparison shows +0.0025, i.e. no structure at all. But only 5 of the 45 unordered pairs in a batch of ten are mirror partners, so the most this design can move the batch mean is about a ninth of that contrast, roughly 0.001 - an order of magnitude below the 0.074 announcement-to-announcement spread. Even a fully structured design that extended the measured pair-level de-correlation to all 45 pairs would buy about 0.006, still a sixteenth of the 0.098 excess similarity the buy carries over its own field. That is a quantitative ceiling on the whole family of base-sample designs for this allocator at batch ten, and it was obtained without spending a position on a pair-count sweep. The mechanism of the failure is also measured, and it is more general than the node: the allocator consumes a masked argmax, which is insensitive to the sign of the residual. Mirroring reduces the variance of linear and monotone functionals, but both members of a pair sit above the mean-only maximum at different candidates, so the within-pair spread of the sampled maxima (0.0245) is as large as the spread between arbitrary rows (0.0226), and the number of distinct candidates the ten rows prefer is unchanged at 7.680 against the Parent's 7.678. Variance reduction on the inputs does not reach a decision taken by an argmax; any future attempt at this on this host has to act on a functional the allocation actually reads - a set-level ranking or batch objective, or a surrogate that scores a candidate set - not on the arrangement of the base rows. Where the redundancy does live is upstream of the draw. The buy's excess over its field held at 0.097-0.098 across both arms while the absolute level tracked the field, and the Molecular reading of this node shows why: 231-555 distinct Murcko scaffolds across the 870 proposals of a task collapse to 6-27 in the best forty, with 71 percent of one seed's final hundred proposals sharing a single scaffold, and 13-20 proposals per task are three heavy atoms or fewer while up to a quarter of a set scores below a tenth of the running incumbent. The ten picks are alike because the bred field is alike and the mean ranking is narrow, so the method class that could move this observable is a different proposal operator (scaffold-level novelty pressure, an intact-group vocabulary, a destructive-edit screen) or a set-level acquisition, not a different random input. The surrogate is not implicated by this node's evidence: chronological squared error on purchased candidates is 0.0089 against the Parent's 0.0121, both far below the 0.041 archive-mean baseline, though that is measured only on what was bought and says nothing about ranking the unbought field. Two things stay open. The score layer cannot be read here at all: a 0.0377 departure on fifteen cells sits inside the stream-noise band this family already measured, and this node changes stream consumption by construction, so no part of the panel can be attributed to the design. And the result closes this hypothesis about this host's purchase redundancy, not variance-reduced sampling in general: a scrambled-net or otherwise structured design would change the realized marginals and is a different experiment, while whether the base-sample route is worth another position on this lineage is Search Policy's call on the approach's scope, not this node's.
finding_summary.results: The design itself is beyond doubt: in every one of the 435 announcements of the fifteen matched sessions five rows were drawn and five were their exact negatives, interleaved, with the per-pair negation receipts at exactly zero for both the base rows and the residual matrix, 800 standard normals consumed instead of 1,600, and the pairing independently re-derived from the inherited selection log rather than only from the new receipt. The Parent's law survived the rearrangement as predicted: pooled over all announcements the realized residual variance is 0.990 of the model variance and the pooled base-row second moment is 1.0033, about 1.4 sampling errors from one, while the inherited Cholesky factor, jitter ladder, eligibility mask, sequential masking and first-index ties are provably the Parent's - on the first announcement of all fifteen sessions the drawn rows, the function values they produce and the first purchase are bit-identical to the Parent's. The decision moved too: the two members of a mirror pair prefer different candidates in 4.75 of 5 pairs per announcement, all five differing in 387 of the 435 announcements. What did not happen is the predicted consequence. Mean fragment-excluded within-announcement purchased similarity came out at 0.7085 against the Parent's 0.7054 - a rise of 0.0031 where a fall was registered, with 8 of 15 matched cells falling and 7 rising, inside an announcement-to-announcement spread of 0.074. The field the batch was bought from also became slightly more similar (0.6115 against 0.6071), so the excess similarity of the buy over its own field is 0.0970 against the Parent's 0.0983: essentially unchanged. Realized incumbent-increment mass over the same 4,350 purchases fell to 5.514 against the Parent's 6.080 (264 positive increments against 255), and the late stratum fell to 0.824 against 0.902, so the useful-transfer prediction failed as well; because that quantity telescopes to final minus initial top-1 and the ten initial molecules are identical in every cell, it is exactly fifteen times the score delta and not independent evidence. The complete paired panel is 0.5761 against the Parent's 0.6138, a mean delta of -0.0377 (per seed -0.0677, -0.0016, -0.0439), which is inside this host family's own law-free re-draw band of [-0.055, +0.015] and is therefore reported as no material effect at the score layer rather than a loss; the registered minimum gain of 0.002 was not attained and the node's mean is below the Anchor's 0.6070, so the matched-endpoint-gain criterion is not met. Three cells carry almost the whole departure - the Parent's lucky 0.856 deco_hop cell on seed 0 fell to 0.605, and sitagliptin lost 0.163 on seed 0 and 0.240 on seed 2 - against +0.081 on zaleplon seed 0, with the remaining eleven cells inside 0.036. No technical failure anywhere: three seeds ok, 4,350 accepted purchases, zero invalid or duplicate rejections, zero posterior fallbacks, every factorization succeeding at the first jitter, and the slowest task at 276 s against a 7,200 s limit.

molecular.headline: Flat ring-rich aromatics with zero stereochemistry; the best molecules carry N-halogen, aminal and hypohalite motifs
molecular.overall_character: Across the five trajectory sets this node proposed 870 optimizer molecules per task over seeds 0, 1 and 2 (4,350 in total; the digest records 875-879 unique molecules of 900 read per task, and tasks_without_trajectories is empty, so all five objectives are covered). The chemistry is one family: medium-sized, almost entirely aromatic, heavily ring-fused, neutral and completely flat. The digest's string-level counters support that reading directly - ring_closure_rate 0.9736-0.9828 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9644-0.9793 on every task, mean SMILES length 41.9-69.3, charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five. Read with RDKit 2026.03.3 over the request's trusted trajectory panel (.worktrees/slot-1/runs/staging/seed-{0,1,2}/trajectories/*.jsonl), every one of the 4,350 strings parses, mean heavy-atom count runs 24.2-37.9, mean perceived rings 3.41-5.24 of which 2.06-4.78 are aromatic, and 85.6-96.1 percent of molecules contain a fused ring system. Nothing carries a formal charge and no molecule anywhere specifies a tetrahedral or double-bond configuration, although the highest-scoring subsets carry up to a mean 3.17 unassigned sp3 centres each. What the outputs are missing is not ring chemistry but ordinary medicinal-chemistry vocabulary and stability. Not one of the 4,350 molecules contains a trifluoromethyl group, a fused triazole, or a primary-amine/amide (beta-amino amide) pair; morpholine is absent, piperidine and pyrrolidine appear almost only where the ten fixed starting molecules already supplied them, and six-membered all-sp3 carbocycles occur in at most 1.6 percent of a set. In their place the generator installs motifs that are reagents or transients rather than compounds: halogen bonded directly to nitrogen (21.4 and 38.4 percent of two whole sets, and 55-70 percent of the best forty on those two), halogen bonded to oxygen in hypohalite fashion (16.1 percent of one set), sp3 aminal and hemiaminal-ether carbons (23-27 percent of two sets, 55-68 percent of one best forty), four-membered all-aromatic rings (77.5 percent of one best forty) and all-aromatic rings of seven to ten atoms (17.5 percent of another best forty). The score gradients do not charge for any of this: two digest molecules differing only N-F versus N-Br score identically at 0.43643070309403553, so a whole axis of the search is chemically meaningless and numerically free. Diversity is real but front-loaded: 231-555 distinct Murcko scaffolds across the 870 proposals of a task, collapsing to 6-27 scaffolds in the best forty, and on one task 71 percent of a seed's final hundred proposals shared a single scaffold. A measurable slice of the budget also goes to collapsed fragments - 13 to 20 proposals per task have three or fewer heavy atoms, including single-atom strings, and late proposals an order of magnitude below the running incumbent reach 24.8 percent of one set. Comparison basis: context.comparison records a complete Child evaluation on seeds 0, 1, 2 and complete Parent pairing against n-f28be8ac3d12, with no missing trajectory. I read the Parent through its published anonymized view, runs/SPIRAL2/policy/views/n-f28be8ac3d12/seed-{0,1,2}/trajectories/objective-{A..E}.jsonl, rather than the raw node directory. Measured the same way, the Parent's output is the same chemistry: the same fused flat aromatics, the same total absence of specified stereochemistry and formal charge, the same N-halogen habit (43.1 and 51.7 percent on two of its sets) and the same aminergic amine-plus-phenol series where an objective rewards it. The differences I can see between the arms are which series a given seed settled into, not a new kind of chemistry - consistent with an intervention on the allocation draw rather than on the generator, though whether the mechanism activated is not mine to judge. All measurements here are read-only recomputations from the trusted panel and the digest; no derived file was published into the run.

per_task.generated_character: Small, flat tricyclics. Digest counters: 870 optimizer molecules, mean SMILES length 41.9 (max 90), aromatic_atom_rate 0.9782, ring_closure_rate 0.9793, halogen_rate 0.8149, charged_rate 0.0, stereocentre_rate 0.0; score span 0.0-0.4562. Measured over the trajectory panel: mean 24.2 heavy atoms, MW 347, 3.45 perceived rings of which 2.74 aromatic, 95.6 percent fused, clogP 3.91, TPSA 58. The recurring body is a pyrrolo-fused aza-aromatic (indolizine/pyrrolopyridine type) whose third ring is closed by a one-atom CH2 or N-CH2-O bridge across the aromatic plate, decorated with methyl and methoxy, and bearing at the 2-position a ketone, an aryl amide or an N-aryl urea ending in phenyl or pyridyl: the best molecule is Cc1c2nc3c(cc(C(=O)CCc4ccccn4)n3CO2)c1C at 0.4562. Aryl amide or urea is present in 72.5 percent of the best forty, and 50 percent carry a pyridine. The whole series is achiral and uncharged; 305 distinct Murcko scaffolds over the set narrow to 16 in the best forty.
liabilities: N-halogen amides and ureas in 55 percent of the best forty, e.g. N(F)C(=O)N(C)aryl and N(Br)C(=O)N(C)aryl, which are halogenating reagents rather than stable compounds
the N-CH2-O bridge that closes the third ring is an aminal, hydrolytically labile, and it sits in the best molecule of the task
free NH imines or amidines in 31.5 percent of the set, including the last proposal COc1c(C)c2cc3c1cc(C(=N)Cc1ccccn1)n3CO2, which would tautomerise or hydrolyse
95 percent of the best forty contain an aromatic atom shared by three rings, i.e. peri-fused or one-atom-bridged aromatic plates that are strained rather than ordinary fused heteroaromatics
a sulfenamide S-N bond in 4.8 percent of the set and a thiol in 5.2 percent
missing_features: no aromatic nitrile anywhere in the series: 1 of 870 proposals carries C#N, and none of the best forty
five-membered aromatic azole rings nearly vanish from the best forty, 0.05 against 0.368 over the whole set, so no azole-fused diazine core was ever assembled
no saturated or sp3-rich ring attached to the aromatic core: pyrrolidine, piperidine and morpholine are all 0.0 of 870
no specified stereochemistry and no sp3 stereocentre at all in the best forty, so the series explores only one flat shape
no acidic or strongly polar handle: carboxylic acid and sulfonamide are both 0.0 of 870
no trifluoromethyl group despite halogen_rate 0.8149, so fluorine enters only as single ring or N substituents
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient is a size-and-fusion ramp that then rewards one decoration pattern. The worst molecules are literal fragments scoring exactly 0.0 (NF, C, NN, FCl, C=NC=CC=CF); the bottom forty average 15.1 heavy atoms and 1.77 rings, the best forty 24.3 heavy atoms and 3.95 rings with 100 percent fusion and TPSA falling from 58 to 45.9. per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient rewards fluorine placed anywhere, including places it cannot sit. N-halogen rises from 0.384 over the set to 0.70 in the best forty, gem-difluoro appears in 20 percent of the best forty, and the whole best forty carries the same imidazole- or pyrazole-fused dione core (1.00 versus 0.728 over the set). Size separates the ends sharply - bottom forty 9.4 heavy atoms and MW 142 against 26.5 and MW 377 - and the span behaves multiplicatively, the digest worst being 7.3e-28: two consecutive seed-2 proposals, evaluations 296 and 297, score 0.3747 and 0.00014953, the second being the ring-opened C=C(F)OC(=N)n1ccn(C)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)cc1S. 50.5 percent of all proposals score below half the running incumbent and 24.8 percent below a tenth of it, the worst such ratio of the five sets, and two of three seeds spent their last hundred evaluations inside one scaffold (71 and 42 percent single-scaffold share) ending at 0.603 and 0.481 against seed 1's 0.715.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 for all five trajectory sets, and no molecule among the 4,350 proposals carries a tetrahedral or double-bond tag. Yet on one task the best forty average 3.17 unassigned sp3 centres with 100 percent carrying at least one, and two further tasks average 1.20 and 0.45 in their best forty. The highest-scoring molecules are therefore undefined mixtures of up to eight diastereomers presented as one candidate.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never emits stereochemistry, although its own best molecules are full of undefined sp3 centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Candidate construction and mutation work on a flat graph: configuration is neither inherited nor edited, so no endpoint that depends on three-dimensional fit can be addressed and no two enantiomers can ever be distinguished. A generator that enumerated or mutated configuration at sp3 centres would make a currently invisible axis of the space reachable, at the cost of treating stereoisomers as distinct candidates in the population and in any similarity or redundancy statistic.

transferable_gaps.evidence: N-halogen bonds appear in 21.4 and 38.4 percent of two whole sets and in 55 and 70 percent of their best forty; O-halogen hypohalite bonds appear in 16.1 percent of a third set and 12.5 percent of its best forty, including the OCOCOCl group in that set's top-scoring molecule. Two digest molecules that differ only N-F versus N-Br score the identical 0.43643070309403553, so the substitution is numerically free and chemically meaningless.
transferable_gaps.gap: Halogen is attached directly to nitrogen and to oxygen, and the search spends real budget on that axis for no score change.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The atom-substitution operator treats halogen as attachable to any heteroatom, and nothing downstream charges for it, so a whole neighbourhood of the proposal distribution consists of halogenating reagents rather than compounds. Restricting halogen attachment to carbon, or giving heteroatom-halogen edits no proposal mass, would redirect that fraction of each batch to edits that can change the score, without any knowledge of which endpoint is being optimised.

transferable_gaps.evidence: N-C-N sp3 aminals appear in 27.0 and 23.0 percent of two whole sets and in 55 percent of one best forty; hemiaminal ethers reach 67.5 percent and halogen on a carbon bearing nitrogen 40 percent of that same best forty. On another task the one-atom N-CH2-O bridge that closes the third ring sits in the single highest-scoring molecule of the set.
transferable_gaps.gap: Bonds are closed through heteroatom-substituted sp3 carbons, producing aminals, hemiaminal ethers and alpha-halo amines as load-bearing motifs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Fragment joining and ring closure choose attachment atoms by graph position alone, with no constraint that the new sp3 carbon not carry two heteroatoms. The result is that the generator's best output is systematically hydrolytically labile. A stability constraint on the newly formed carbon, or a preference for carbon-carbon closure, would change the character of every high-scoring series it produces.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Four-membered all-aromatic rings occur in 7.6 percent of one whole set and 77.5 percent of its best forty; all-aromatic rings of seven to ten atoms occur in 18.6 and 19.3 percent of two sets and 17.5 percent of another best forty, with perceived ring sizes of 8, 9 and 10 among the highest-scoring molecules. Exocyclic methylene on an aromatic carbon reaches 70 percent of one best forty.
transferable_gaps.gap: The ring-closure operator creates ring sizes and fusion patterns that no aromatic system supports.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring formation is a string or graph operation checked only by the parser, which accepts antiaromatic four-rings, medium aromatic rings and quinone-methide forms. Because the optimizer then climbs on whatever scores, these degenerate topologies become the dominant family at the top of a run and crowd out makeable series that reach almost the same value - on one task a chemically ordinary series reached within 0.010 of the cage-like best. Constraining new aromatic rings to five and six atoms with ordinary fusion would move that competition back to compounds.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Not one of the 4,350 molecules contains a trifluoromethyl group, although digest halogen_rate is 0.79 to 0.98 on four of the five sets. Sulfonamide is 0.0 on four sets, carboxylic acid 0.0 or below 0.006 on four, digest charged_rate is 0.0 everywhere, and fused triazole is 0.0 everywhere. On the set whose gradient most clearly rewards fluorine, the generator instead reached its best values through N-F and single fluoromethyl substituents.
transferable_gaps.gap: The fragment vocabulary has no prefabricated polar or perfluorinated groups: halogen enters one atom at a time.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The mutation alphabet is per-atom, so a group that only pays off assembled - CF3, a sulfonamide, a carboxylate, a fused azole - is three or four simultaneous edits away and effectively unreachable. Adding a small library of intact functional groups to the proposal alphabet would give the same loop access to regions it cannot currently enter, with no change to how candidates are valued.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Morpholine is 0.0 across all five sets; piperidine is at most 0.201 and pyrrolidine at most 0.176, both on the sets whose ten starting molecules already contained those rings, and both fall to 0.0 in the corresponding best forty; six-membered all-sp3 carbocycles reach at most 1.6 percent of a set. Measured aromatic ring counts are 2.06 to 4.78 of 3.41 to 5.24 total rings, and digest aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9644 to 0.9793.
transferable_gaps.gap: Saturated and sp3-rich ring chemistry is absent unless the fixed starting molecules supplied it.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator can decorate and fuse flat aromatics but cannot saturate a ring or build an aliphatic ring system de novo, so the shape distribution of its output is one-dimensional. Carrying saturated ring fragments and a ring-saturation move would widen the accessible shape space without touching the acquisition or valuation steps.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Basic amine rates over the whole sets are 0.039, 0.051 and 0.103 on three tasks and 0.634 and 0.756 on the two whose starting population or early incumbents carried an amine. On those two the best forty reach 1.00 and 0.85, so the amine is the single feature most associated with the top of the range; on the other three the best forty contain 0.0, 0.0 and 0.275. Aryl piperazine, the canonical basic ring, is 0.069 of a set and 0.0 of its best forty.
transferable_gaps.gap: Basic amine centres are inherited, not invented, although where they are present they dominate the best molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A protonatable amine on a ring system is one of the highest-value features in this generator's own output, and it appears only by inheritance from the fixed initial molecules. The generator has no move that installs a basic nitrogen onto a scaffold that lacks one, so three of five starting populations determined once and for all that the feature was unavailable for the rest of the run.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each set contains 13 to 20 proposals of three or fewer heavy atoms - C, O, F, NF, NN, FCl, CSS, C#C, Cl, Br among them - and 15 to 27 of eight or fewer. Across a run, 50.5 percent of one set's proposals and 17.1 percent of another's score below half the running incumbent, and 24.8 percent and 4.6 percent below a tenth of it; on one task every seed was still proposing zero-scoring molecules inside its final hundred evaluations. Only 3.2 to 10.0 percent of proposals improved the incumbent at all.
transferable_gaps.gap: Destructive edits are never filtered: the loop keeps buying one- and two-atom fragments and molecules far below its own incumbent.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Mutation can delete most of a molecule and the resulting fragment is still proposed, scored and charged to the oracle budget, because nothing between the operator and the batch rejects a candidate that is smaller than any plausible answer. A size or heavy-atom floor on proposals, or any late re-proposal screen, would return a measurable slice of the evaluation budget to candidates that can compete with the incumbent.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
